title: Let client and agency coding agents share one app safely
summary: An agency owner built CommonForge, a free, openly shared tool that lets client and agency coding agents work on one app safely; no usage results are given.
agent_role: Client and agency coding agents make changes in parallel in per-task repos; the system catches conflicts and holds changes in staging until they are cleared before production.
outcome: Author says it is open source (MIT) and deploys into your own Cloudflare account with one script; no usage results stated.
what_they_did: An agency owner noticed that clients now build working software with AI. So they built CommonForge to let client agents and agency agents work on the same app. Each task gets its own separate code storage on Cloudflare, holding only the code that task needs. Client logins can't reach the agency's behind-the-scenes systems. Every change goes to a test copy of the app before the live version.
how_it_went: The author shares an 8-minute demo. They say the tool is free to use and change, and it installs into your own Cloudflare account with one script. No usage results are given.
worth_knowing: The main safety idea to borrow: each agent sees only the code its task needs, and client agents are kept away from the agency's behind-the-scenes systems.
prompt: Help me set up a workflow where outside contributors' coding agents and my own agents can work on [project] in parallel. Propose a structure where each task gets its own repo or branch containing only the code it needs, outside credentials cannot reach [backend services], conflicts are detected before merge, and every change deploys to staging first. Show me the plan and any access changes before applying them, and never deploy to production without my approval.

curation.rationale: A real agency problem — client and agency coding agents working on the same app — solved with an open-source setup and a demo, but the post mostly lists features and gives no results.
